rationale:
Evidence: iteration 5 (base_speed 1.8, kp 2.8, ki 0.3, kd 0.4, last_direction, sensors at y 0.06 with x from -0.06 to +0.06, 16 mm footprints, body 0.18 x 0.12 m, 0.8 kg) is the best measured design at 137.76. It beats the iteration 2 and 4 baseline (132.00, base 1.6) by 5.76. The raced outcome table and the iteration 5 produced entity both give kp 2.8, so I use kp 2.8. The kp 3.0 figure in the authorized text and in several critiques is a documentation error.

What I accepted from the round-2 critique: (1) This iteration is a score-preserving resubmission, not a learning test, and I say so here. Seed and track fix the disturbance, so the race should reproduce 137.76. Iteration 4 reproduced iteration 2 exactly, which supports this. (2) The max_error trigger cannot discriminate, because every off-track run is capped at the 0.06 m limit. I drop it as a decision input. (3) The progress losses on the s-bend (0.27 to 0.18) and slalom (0.16 to 0.12) at base 1.8 are real, and they are the main cost of the speed change. The oval time term is worth only about 20 points, so speed is kept for the oval finish and not for the time bonus.

What I rejected: (a) Reverting to base 1.6 now, since that adds no information and is 5.8 points lower. (b) Changing kp, ki, kd or geometry in this race, which would give up the best measured score for an untested design. (c) The round-2 claim that kp 2.8 and kd 1.0 were 'shown to add no gain'. Those values were never raced, so I do not rely on that claim. (d) Lowering speed for the time bonus, since completion is worth 500 points.

What I changed: nothing relative to iteration 5. Expected result: score about 137.8, oval progress about 0.55 with the occasional finish, s-bend and slalom progress near 0.18 and 0.12, and off-track ends on nearly every run.

Decision rule for the next round: if the race reproduces 137.76, the next single-variable test is ki 0.1 (not 1.0) to probe steady bias, with success judged on score and on s-bend and slalom progress, not max_error. If s-bend and slalom progress is the main loss, test a sensor footprint or span change on those tracks. Base_speed 2.0 is the next speed step only if completion_time, not off-track ends, is the limit.
